missing_features: No pagination/offset/cursor on any list endpoint — tickets default to LIMIT 200, customers LIMIT 50, wallet LIMIT 200 with no way to page through results
No DELETE routes for customers, services, technicians, rooms — only soft delete via active=0 but no dedicated DELETE endpoint
No refund functionality — wallet_transactions schema includes 'refund' type but no route to process refunds
No appointment/scheduling system — cannot pre-book time slots or reserve services
No reporting/analytics API — dashboard only shows live today data, no historical revenue trends, financial summaries, or period reports
No export functionality — no CSV/Excel/JSON export for tickets, customers, revenue, or any business data
No discount/promotion/coupon system — no way to apply price adjustments or promotions to tickets
No inventory/product management — no tracking of products sold alongside services
No expense tracking — no costs, rent, utilities, or profit margin calculation
No ticket transfer between technicians — cannot reassign an active ticket
No partial/split payment — tickets are paid in full only
No customer loyalty/reward program beyond basic balance — no points, tiers, or rewards
No employee shift management or break scheduling
No multi-shop data isolation — shop_id is accepted from request but not validated against user's shop on most routes
No notification history or log endpoint for sent notifications
No backup/restore API despite having a backup module in the codebase
No API versioning — all routes under /api/ with no /api/v1/ prefix
No OpenAPI/Swagger documentation endpoint
No search/filter on reviews by date range or rating threshold
No customer visit history or service history endpoint
No technician availability/schedule view
No queue management for walk-in customers
performance_issues: No pagination on list endpoints causes large result sets — /api/tickets returns up to 200 rows, /api/customers 50 rows per request
N+1 query pattern in getTicketWithJoins — runs a separate JOIN query for each ticket detail fetch instead of batch loading
No caching layer — services, rooms, technicians, and other reference data are queried from database every single request
AI scoring endpoint loops sequentially through all technicians with await — O(n) latency where n is technician count; should be parallelized
/api/ai/chat loads ALL today's tickets into memory with SELECT * FROM tickets WHERE created_at>=? — could be very large for busy shops
customers search uses LIKE '%${q}%' causing full table scans with no full-text index or trigram search
Dashboard /api/dashboard/live runs 3 separate heavy queries (techs, rooms, stats) that could be optimized or combined
No database connection pooling — better-sqlite3 is synchronous single-threaded with no read optimization
wallet_transactions table lacks an index on shop_id, making shop-filtered queries slow
No query builder or prepared statement reuse — every route constructs SQL strings inline, missing SQLite statement caching benefits
Rate limiter uses in-memory Map — resets on every restart and doesn't work across multiple processes
getTicketWithJoins is called multiple times in the same ticket flow (create, pay, status change) — each call is a separate query
No query limit enforcement on /api/ai/chats — limit is capped at 200 but no offset for deep history
All tickets for today are loaded in the AI chat context even when only summary stats are needed
reviews listing has no index on (technician_id, created_at) for the common 'recent reviews for technician' query pattern
security_gaps: No role-based access control (RBAC) — any authenticated user can access /api/tickets, /api/customers, /api/users, /api/shops regardless of role
No multi-tenancy enforcement — shop_id from request body/query is never validated against req.user.shop_id, allowing cross-shop data access
No IDOR protection — /api/customers/:id, /api/tickets/:id, /api/reviews expose resources without ownership/shop verification
CORS set to origin: true — allows any origin to access the API with credentials
Server listens on 0.0.0.0 — exposed to all network interfaces with no IP whitelisting option
Default credentials seeded as admin/admin and pos/pos — well-known default passwords in the database seed
No CSRF protection on any endpoint — cookies/tokens accepted without CSRF tokens
No HTTPS enforcement — server operates over plain HTTP
Only /api/auth/login is rate-limited — all other endpoints (especially /api/auth/password reset, /api/customers POST) have no rate limiting
No account lockout mechanism after repeated failed login attempts
JWT secret defaults to 'yuwen-spa-default-secret-change-me' — hardcoded fallback secret
JWT has no refresh token mechanism — 7-day tokens with no rotation
No input validation/sanitization library — req.body values are used directly in SQL and business logic without schema validation
No audit logging for most operations — only ticket.pay creates audit_logs; customer/service/technician CRUD operations are not audited
Webhook URLs stored in plain text in technicians table — no encryption at rest
AI config endpoint (/api/ai/config) returns configuration without auth role check — anyone with a token can read it
/api/reviews is completely public (no auth required) — anyone can submit reviews without authentication
No file upload validation — technician avatar field exists but no validation on file type/size
No request logging middleware — no structured audit trail of who did what and when
No Content-Security-Policy enforcement on API responses
Error messages may leak internal details — e.g., UNIQUE constraint errors expose database structure
Password minimum length is only 4 characters — far below security best practices
code_quality_issues: Duplicate startOfDay() function defined in 4+ files (tickets.js, technicians.js, dashboard.js, ai.js) — should be a shared utility
No consistent response format — some endpoints return raw objects, others wrap in { ok: true }, some return arrays, inconsistent error shapes
SQL construction via string concatenation is fragile and hard to maintain — no query builder, no template safety
Inconsistent error handling — some routes use try-catch, others throw without catching, changeStatus() has no try-catch at all
Fire-and-forget notification calls with .catch(()=>{}) silently swallow all errors — no logging or retry mechanism
No TypeScript — zero type safety across the entire codebase
No test suite — no unit, integration, or end-to-end tests visible in the project
No environment variable management — JWT_SECRET falls back to hardcoded default, database path is hardcoded
Magic numbers everywhere — limit defaults (200, 50), password minimum (4), commission calculations, token expiry all hardcoded
No middleware pipeline for auth validation — the auth hook runs but there's no pre-validation middleware for request bodies
The customers PUT endpoint includes 'tags' in the updatable fields but never JSON-parses it — tags will be stored as a string, not an array
No database transaction isolation handling — transaction() calls don't handle SQLITE_BUSY errors gracefully
No API versioning strategy — breaking changes will have no migration path
notify/index.js and ai/agent.js modules have no visible error handling for failed external calls
No structured logging — relies on Fastify's default logger with no request-level audit trail
The 'limit' query parameter is never validated to be within reasonable bounds — a client could request LIMIT 1000000
Missing updated_at timestamps on some operations (e.g., topup doesn't update customer.updated_at)
No consistent use of reply objects — some routes use return directly, others use reply.code().send()
